title: No pass by default
statement: No check passes by default when what it inspects or needs is missing, because otherwise leaving a part out becomes the easiest way to pass.
example: Two automatic passes for leaving out the source lifted first-try pass rates from about 50% to 76-92% on three item types.
detail: Red-team runs against a content judge found that an item with no source earned two automatic passes, "no stimulus = PASS" and "N/A → pass", and that leaving the source out moved first-try rates from about 50% to 76-92% on three item types (`icloud-work/aptraining/Cheater/reports/FINAL_REPORT.md`; `icloud-work/aptraining/Cheater/from_cheater/SINGLE_IB_GRADE_SURVIVAL_GUIDE.md`). It also switched off the judge's costliest check, the one for answers a student could reach without the subject knowledge, which runs only when a source is present (`icloud-work/aptraining/Cheater/reports/RUBRIC_BLINDSPOTS.md`). A reading of the same judge's code found that when its curriculum reference came back empty it kept grading rather than failing the row, and its alignment checks default-passed on the missing data (`icloud-work/aptraining/workspace/comms/_deprecated/outboxes/from_research/2026-04-28T1240Z_R29_ib_curriculum_503_findings.md`). A missing required part fails the item, a judge without its reference gives no verdict, and 'not applicable' is recorded apart from 'pass'.
against: Some item types legitimately have no source, so what counts as required has to come from each type's specification: "Many textbook drills and formative-assessment items omit stimuli for the same reason (faster recall practice)." (`icloud-work/aptraining/Cheater/exploits/EXPLOIT-002-stimulus-strip.md`, lines 212-214). items without a source are legitimate for quick recall practice, as the exploit study itself notes. On fresh items the source-free version passed 45 of 50, 90%, only 4 points above the raw model's 86% (icloud-work/aptraining/artifacts/second_tier/2026-05-22T1715Z_cheater_exploit_002_stimulus_strip/cheater_validation_verdict.md, line 3; icloud-work/aptraining/artifacts/second_tier/2026-05-22T1715Z_cheater_exploit_002_stimulus_strip/SECOND_TIER_REASON.md, line 10). Source-free items suit stem-only practice drills (same file, line 19), and the project's own generator checklist said '- [ ] If unsure of a source — drop the stimulus, write a non-stimulus item' (icloud-work/aptraining/helpers/shadow/output/ib_satisfaction_kit_v1/generator_prompts/common_pre_checklist.md, line 24).
